title: Size bounded by two to the depth
statement: Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, with size (number of leaves) $\mathrm{size}(T)$ and depth $\mathrm{depth}(T)$. Then $\mathrm{size}(T) \le 2^{\mathrm{depth}(T)}$; that is, a decision tree of depth $k$ has at most $2^{k}$ leaves.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables
replaced:
Every decision tree satisfies $T.\mathrm{size} \le 2^{T.\mathrm{depth}}$: a tree of depth
$k$ has at most $2^k$ leaves.
